<!-- pr-reviewer: 805375bf4bf35149ada4225919ebea087223455f -->

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

What looks good:
- The verdict reuses `pick::winding::winding_of`. The importer and the face picks agree on what "inward" means. The module carries a provenance comment: signed volume by the divergence theorem (Zhang & Chen, ICIP 2001) and the manifold test from published literature. Clean-room holds.
- Only a closed, manifold, consistently wound body with a clearly negative volume turns. An open, non-manifold, mixed, or flat body stays as the file says. Unit tests and the fixture tests pin each of those cases.
- The turn is said: `Graded::notes` feed `ImportModel::notes`, the script and MCP `import` result, and the UI status line. Tests pin the MCP path and the status-line path. A plain import says nothing.
- The hand-resolved merge was checked with `git show --remerge-diff`. Both sides stay in all five files. Nothing from main is dropped. Main's `parse_noted` plumbing keeps one copy, and this PR's note extends it. The change to `a_lone_curved_face_is_left_alone` keeps its point: the lone face is open again through a `SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL`, and the mirror-normal assert still proves the importer left both windings alone.
- The pinning tests are not vacuous. Without the fix the inverted box imports with a negative volume and empty notes, and the asserts fail.
- `docs/decisions/1617-step-inward-shell.md` records the choice, the alternatives, and the overlap with #1576. No new cross-crate dependency. All files stay under 400 lines. `unwrap()` and `expect()` appear only in tests.

Results, on the self-hosted runner (pr-test.yml run 43614730968, macOS, against main `389fe96c`):
- Trial merge with main: clean.
- Quick gate on the merged tree: 0 failed. The plan ran the `import_step_outward` suite whole, the `camcraft-app` lib tests (the `step_outward` unit tests), the `camcraft-ui` lib tests (the status-line test), and the import, mcp, step, model-fidelity, and ui suites from the gate map.
- Clippy `-p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised (this is a safety-floor review):
- The local test part `step-block-371.step` named in the issue. It is not in the repository. The synthetic reversed `box.step` stands in.
- STL or OBJ bodies wound inward. This PR does not change those importers.
- The heights checks against a turned model. The audit comment on the issue covers pencil, deburr, geodesic, and the sign-folded readers, and says the heights were not examined.
- The batch tier. `post-merge.yml` runs it when this merges.

Notes (not blockers):
- The issue comment says an inward STL or OBJ body can still reach the facet-normal readers in `crates/motion` (pencil, deburr). Consider a follow-up issue for those importers.
- The runner checked the macOS arm only. The diff adds no OS-pinned reading, so no local re-run was owed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
